$NFLX

“Netflix doesn’t produce quality content anymore.”

This is a fair argument in comparison to the likes of Paramount. It's impossible to deny that Paramount has produced some of the BEST series over the last 10 years – all thanks to one man...

Taylor Sheridan. 

Interestingly enough, he has decided to depart his exclusive agreement with paramount and sign a long-term "frictionless no-minimum" production deal with NBCUniversal. Interesting.

Comcast - the parent of NBCU - just announced splitting the business into segments, aiming for mid 2027 completion. This would put NBCU in a camp with...

- NBC Studios
- Bravo (Cable TV)
- Peacock Streaming (Sports)
- Skynews + NBC Broadcasting
- Licensing for NFL, NBA, Premier League, etc..
- Universal Parks

Previously speculated, to me, NBCU is a fantastic acquisition target. Obviously Netflix would not be interesting in the parks or Broadcasting generally speaking, though it's not crazy to see some sort of negotiated split or partition of the undesired assets.

Immediately, Netflix solves a multiple of issues:

1. Quality content (Sheridan).
2. LiveTV integrations (Peacock).
3. LiveSports licensing for major leagues.
4. Amazing IP/Studios.

Analysts have suspected that such a deal could be pulled off for $44-60B USD, which is 25-50% less than the estimated $83B deal Netflix attempted to pull off for Paramount/WarnerBros.

Do-able.

All said, I think this would be brilliant business for Netflix if such an opportunity arises in 2027. As an investor, we would see the narrative flip on the company quite quickly once we had sufficient commentary on the subject.

Forward P/E: 17x
FCF Yield: 4.5%
P/FCF: 22x

At these valuations, I think $NFLX is really great value. Though, sub-$60 (below 20x P/FCF) would be tremendous value.

Keep your eyes and ears open. I think $NFLX is one acquisition away from +20% top-line growth once again.
